We have carbon NMR data: chemical shifts: 139.25, 134.60, 129.00, 129.00, 128.30, 128.30, 49.40, 26.10, 11.40 ppm.

We need number of CH3 groups in the compound. Methyl carbon typically appears around 10-15 ppm for aliphatic CH3 attached to carbon (e.g., methyl attached to aromatic maybe ~20). Here we have a signal at 11.40 ppm, likely a CH3. Also 26.10 ppm could be CH2 or CH3 attached to something else (like isopropyl). 49.40 ppm could be a carbon attached to heteroatom or a CH (maybe CH). Aromatic carbons are 128-140 region.

We need count of CH3 groups. Use DEPT? Not available. Could use proton NMR to see methyl signals. Let's get proton NMR.
